9351 Craniopharyngioma, adamantinomatous - the childhood subtype. Wet keratin, calcification and cysts with machinery-oil fluid; nuclear beta-catenin is diagnostic and reflects a CTNNB1 mutation. Recurs after subtotal resection, and hypothalamic and endocrine morbidity dominate the outcome.
9401 Astrocytoma, anaplastic. Mitotically active astrocytoma without the necrosis or microvascular proliferation that would make it 9440 Glioblastoma, NOS.

9392 Ependymoma, anaplastic. Grade is the whole of the distinction from 9391 Ependymoma, NOS: brisk mitoses, microvascular proliferation, necrosis. WHO CNS5 no longer grades ependymoma by histology alone in every compartment, so record what the report states rather than re-grading it.

9505 Ganglioglioma, anaplastic at behaviour /3. Anaplasia is in the glial component - brisk mitoses, microvascular proliferation, necrosis, high Ki-67 in the glial areas. The behaviour digit is the whole distinction from ganglioglioma at /1.

notes: A related term of 9474 Large cell medulloblastoma. Marked nuclear pleomorphism, cell-cell wrapping and high mitotic and apoptotic counts.
9530 Meningioma, malignant at behaviour /3. Anaplastic and malignant are the same grade-3 category.

9382 Oligoastrocytoma, NOS with the grade recorded separately. Retired by WHO CNS5 for the same reason as oligoastrocytoma. Code it from a pre-2021 file and annotate that no molecular testing was available.

full_form: Oligodendroglioma, anaplastic, NOS -> Oligodendroglioma, anaplastic, NOS (9451)
notes: 9451 Oligodendroglioma, anaplastic, NOS, CNS WHO grade 3. WHO CNS5 requires IDH mutation plus 1p/19q codeletion; where molecular testing is unavailable, code from the report and record at least the IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry result if it was done.

9431 Angiocentric glioma, CNS WHO grade 1. Elongated bipolar cells arranged around vessels; EMA positive in a dot-like or ring-like pattern, GFAP positive, OLIG2 positive. Cortical, usually frontal or temporal, and epilepsy is the presentation. A MYB::QKI fusion is characteristic - the fusion is written with the double colon and is reproduced exactly. Excellent outcome after gross total resection.
9534 Angiomatous meningioma at behaviour /0. More than half the tumour is vessels; often marked oedema on imaging. CNS WHO grade 1, and not a vascular tumour.

9430 Astroblastoma. ICD-O-3.2 marks the term 'Astroblastoma' [obs]; it does not retire the code. 9430 appears in no IARC deleted-code list, which is where a retired number is recorded. WHO CNS5 recognises astroblastoma, MN1-altered; DNA methylation profiling establishes it and MN1 break-apart FISH supports it. Below that, code 9430/3 and report the astroblastic PATTERN rather than the entity. Topography does not move this code: 9430 is IIId3 across Group III.

also_known_as: High-grade neuroepithelial tumour with MN1 alteration
notes: The WHO CNS5 preferred name for 9430. ICD-O-3.2 carries no such string — its only term on the code is 'Astroblastoma', which IARC marks [obs] — so this name reaches the clerk through the diagnosis line, not as the ICD-O term. Established by DNA methylation profiling; MN1 break-apart FISH at 38% or more of nuclei against a control of about 9% supports it without establishing it.

A descriptive label in circulation locally against a glioma code. It means an astrocytoma, so it resolves to 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS, not to 9380 Glioma, malignant. The supratentorial pathway is entered because every astrocytoma code is reachable there, but the compartment should be set from the actual site - a cerebellar astrocytoma is usually 9421 Pilocytic astrocytoma and belongs in the posterior fossa pathway. Grade and subtype then narrow it to 9401 Astrocytoma, anaplastic, 9411 Gemistocytic astrocytoma, NOS, 9420 Fibrillary astrocytoma, 9424 Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma or 9425 Pilomyxoid astrocytoma.

notes: 9390 Atypical choroid plexus papilloma at behaviour /1, CNS WHO grade 2. Defined by raised mitotic count rather than by the other atypical features. The behaviour digit is the only thing separating it from the papilloma and the carcinoma.

9539 Atypical meningioma at behaviour /1, CNS WHO grade 2. Four or more mitoses per 10 high-power fields, or brain invasion, or three of the five minor criteria. Brain invasion alone is enough - that changed in WHO 2016 and is the commonest reason a meningioma is undergraded. The same code at /3 is 9539 Meningeal sarcomatosis, so confirm the behaviour.

full_form: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor -> Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (9508)
notes: 9508 Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor. Loss of nuclear INI1 (SMARCB1), or rarely BRG1 (SMARCA4), is the diagnostic finding and immunohistochemistry is enough to make it. It spans compartments - about half of infant cases are infratentorial, which is why this alias enters the posterior fossa pathway, but it also occurs supratentorially, in the sellar region and in the cord. Loss of INI1 is an indication for germline SMARCB1 testing in rhabdoid tumour predisposition syndrome.

A site description covering several entities. Code 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS where the tumour is astrocytic, 9380 Glioma, malignant where the report says only glioma, and 9421 Pilocytic astrocytoma for a dorsally exophytic or tectal tumour with that histology. Topography decides the subgroup: 9380 Glioma, malignant is IIIb at C72.3 optic nerve and IIId2 at every other Group III site; outside C70.0-C72.9, C75.1 and C75.3 it leaves Group III altogether.

9506 Central neurocytoma, CNS WHO grade 2. Lateral ventricle at the foramen of Monro, attached to the septum pellucidum; uniform round cells with a neuropil-like matrix, strongly synaptophysin positive. Its clear-cell look is why it is mistaken for an oligodendroglioma - synaptophysin settles it.

full_form: CNS embryonal tumor, NOS -> CNS embryonal tumor, NOS (9473)
notes: A related term of 9473 CNS embryonal tumor, NOS. The local option list carries this string, which is not the ICD-O-3.2 preferred term, but the code behind it is right. Topography decides the group: 9473 CNS embryonal tumor, NOS is IIIc2 only for an intracranial or intraspinal primary; a peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumour belongs to Group VIII or Group IX.

A site description still common in referral letters. Most cerebellar astrocytomas in children are 9421 Pilocytic astrocytoma; if the histology does not support that, code 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS. Do not code it to a glioma code on the strength of the word astrocytoma alone.

9480 Cerebellar sarcoma, NOS. ICD-O-3.2 marks the term [obs]; it does not retire the code. The Belgian Cancer Registry's WHO CNS5 coding table assigns Primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant the ICD-O-3.2 code 9480/3, so the number is current. ICCC-3 files 9480 inside the medulloblastoma subgroup IIIc1, which is where a case coded here counts. The tool has no dedicated DICER1-mutant route yet; see docs/TODO.md. Circumscribed arachnoidal cerebellar sarcoma is a synonym of 9471 Desmoplastic nodular medulloblastoma, not of this term.

also_known_as: Chordoid Glioma of the Third Ventricle
notes: 9444 Chordoid glioma. Anterior third ventricle and hypothalamic region, which the supratentorial pathway owns. Cords of epithelioid cells in a mucinous matrix; GFAP, CD34, vimentin and TTF-1 positive, EMA variable, low Ki-67. A PRKCA D463H mutation is characteristic. Slow-growing but hard to resect.

alias: Chordoid glioma of the third ventricle
notes: Full site-qualified name for 9444 Chordoid glioma.

full_form: Choroid plexus carcinoma -> Choroid plexus carcinoma (9390)
notes: 9390 Choroid plexus carcinoma at behaviour /3. All three choroid plexus tumours share code 9390 and are separated by behaviour: /0 papilloma, /1 atypical papilloma, /3 carcinoma. Commonest in the lateral ventricle in infants, which is why this alias enters the supratentorial pathway. A carcinoma in a child is a TP53 germline indication - Li-Fraumeni testing should be offered.

full_form: Choroid plexus papilloma, NOS -> Choroid plexus papilloma, NOS (9390)
notes: 9390 Choroid plexus papilloma, NOS at behaviour /0. If the report says atypical choroid plexus papilloma the same code carries behaviour /1. Confirm the behaviour before coding - the three choroid plexus tumours differ only by it.

8270 Chromophobe adenoma at /0. A tinctorial description from before immunostaining; the modern classification is by pituitary transcription factor. Code it where the report uses it and record any hormone immunohistochemistry.
8270 Chromophobe carcinoma at behaviour /3. Requires demonstrated metastasis.

A related term of 9470 Medulloblastoma, NOS - sheets of small round blue cells without nodularity or anaplasia. Reticulin does not highlight nodules; if it does, the tumour is 9471 Desmoplastic nodular medulloblastoma.

full_form: Clear cell meningioma -> Clear cell meningioma (9538)
notes: 9538 Clear cell meningioma at behaviour /1, CNS WHO grade 2 on its subtype alone. Glycogen-rich clear cells, blocky perivascular collagen; spinal and cerebellopontine-angle sites, and it is one of the meningiomas that does occur in children. SMARCE1 loss is characteristic and germline SMARCE1 testing should be offered. Papillary meningioma sits on the same code at /3.

full_form: Clear cell tumor, NOS -> Clear cell tumor, NOS (8005)
notes: 8005 Clear cell tumor, NOS at behaviour /0; the same code at /3 is 8005 Malignant tumor, clear cell type. A clear cell tumour in the CNS is more often 9506 Central neurocytoma, 9413 Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor or 9538 Clear cell meningioma - use this code only where lineage was not established. Topography decides the group: 8000-8005 are IIIf only at C70.0-C72.9 and C75.1-C75.3; at any other site they belong to Group XII. Behaviour is the second gate - this group declares behaviours 0, 1 and 3 only.

full_form: CNS embryonal tumor, NOS -> CNS embryonal tumor, NOS (9473)
notes: 9473 CNS embryonal tumor, NOS - not a legacy bucket but the live NOS home for the whole new CNS embryonal family. CNS neuroblastoma FOXR2-activated, CNS tumour with BCOR internal tandem duplication, ETMR without a C19MC result and CRINET all fall here when their defining test is unavailable. Record which test was missing. Topography decides the group: 9473 CNS embryonal tumor, NOS is IIIc2 only for an intracranial or intraspinal primary; a peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumour belongs to Group VIII or Group IX.

full_form: Central nervous system tumor, not otherwise specified -> Neoplasm, malignant (8000)
notes: American spelling of CNS tumour NOS. Topography decides the group: 8000-8005 are IIIf only at C70.0-C72.9 and C75.1-C75.3; at any other site they belong to Group XII. Behaviour is the second gate - this group declares behaviours 0, 1 and 3 only.

TPIT-positive, ACTH-expressing pituitary tumour. A benign corticotroph adenoma is 8272 Pituitary adenoma, NOS at /0; 8158 ACTH-producing tumor is coded at /3 and is the code to use where the report itself calls it an ACTH-producing tumour. Topography decides the group: 8158 ACTH-producing tumor and 8290 Oxyphilic adenoma / adenocarcinoma are IIIe1 only at C75.1 pituitary gland; at any other site they belong to Group XI.

notes: Abbreviation for choroid plexus carcinoma: 9390 Choroid plexus carcinoma at /3.

full_form: Central primitive neuroectodermal tumor -> CNS embryonal tumor, NOS (9473)
notes: Abbreviation in the ICD-O-3.2 synonym list for 9473 CNS embryonal tumor, NOS.

full_form: Choroid plexus papilloma -> Choroid plexus papilloma, NOS (9390)
notes: Abbreviation for choroid plexus papilloma: 9390 Choroid plexus papilloma, NOS at /0. Check whether the report qualifies it as atypical, which moves the behaviour to /1.

9350 Craniopharyngioma at behaviour /1 unless the subtype is named: 9351 Craniopharyngioma, adamantinomatous or 9352 Craniopharyngioma, papillary. Almost all childhood cases are adamantinomatous. Registered here because this group registers non-malignant neoplasms - the /1 behaviour is not a reason to leave it out.
The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term on 9351.
The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term on 9352.

A radiological description in circulation locally against a glioma code. It resolves to 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS. A cyst with an enhancing mural nodule in the cerebellum is much more often 9421 Pilocytic astrocytoma - check the site and the histology before settling on the NOS code.

full_form: Desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma -> Desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma (9412)
notes: The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term on 9412, which also covers desmoplastic infantile ganglioglioma.

full_form: Desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma -> Desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma (9412)
notes: 9412 covers both desmoplastic infantile ganglioglioma and desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma; ICD-O-3.2 names the astrocytoma on the code and the ganglioglioma is the same entity with a neuronal component. Large cystic supratentorial mass in an infant with a dural-based solid nodule; desmoplastic stroma, GFAP positive, synaptophysin positive in the ganglion component. Excellent outcome after resection despite its size.

full_form: Desmoplastic nodular medulloblastoma -> Desmoplastic nodular medulloblastoma (9471)
notes: 9471 Desmoplastic nodular medulloblastoma. Reticulin-rich internodular tissue around pale reticulin-free nodules - reticulin is the stain that makes this diagnosis. Commonest in infants and in adults, and the infant nodular form does better than classic medulloblastoma. This code is also where an immunohistochemistry-only site lands an SHH-activated medulloblastoma, through the related term Medulloblastoma, SHH activated, NOS.

full_form: Desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma -> Desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma (9412)
notes: Abbreviation for desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma: 9412.

9400 Astrocytoma, NOS. This is the single most important correction in the group: a file that says diffuse astrocytoma means 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS, not 9380 Glioma, malignant, whatever code the option list has been pairing with the name. Record IDH status if it was tested; where molecular testing is unavailable code 9400 and say so.
In circulation locally against a glioma code. Resolves to 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS; the grade is recorded as a separate data item, not in the morphology code.

full_form: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma -> Astrocytoma, NOS (9400)
notes: A radiological and anatomical diagnosis, not a histological one. Many are never biopsied. Code 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS where there is no molecular result, and 9385 Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant only where H3 K27M is demonstrated. Record the ENCR basis of diagnosis - an imaging-only diagnosis must say so.

full_form: Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant -> Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant (9385)
notes: 9385 Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant only where H3 K27M is demonstrated by immunohistochemistry or sequencing, or K27me3 loss is shown. Without that result the code is 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS and the tumour is recorded as a midline glioma of undetermined H3 status - do not assign the molecular code on site and imaging alone. The pons is the commonest paediatric site, hence the posterior fossa pathway; thalamic and spinal tumours use their own compartments.

full_form: Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant -> Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant (9385)
notes: The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term for 9385, not in local circulation and entered so a search finds it. The marker string H3 K27M is reproduced exactly as written. Requires a demonstrated H3 K27M alteration; otherwise use 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS.

notes: Abbreviation for desmoplastic infantile ganglioglioma: 9412.

full_form: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma -> Astrocytoma, NOS (9400)
notes: Abbreviation for diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma. 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS without tissue or molecular testing; 9385 Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant only on a demonstrated H3 K27M result.

full_form: Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant -> Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant (9385)
notes: Abbreviation for diffuse midline glioma. 9385 Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant only on a demonstrated H3 K27M result; otherwise 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS.

full_form: Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumour -> Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor (9413)
notes: Abbreviation for dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumour: 9413.

full_form: Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor -> Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor (9413)
notes: 9413 Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor, CNS WHO grade 1. The specific glioneuronal element - floating neurons in a myxoid matrix with oligodendroglioma-like cells - is the diagnostic finding. Cortical, usually temporal, bubbly on T2 and FLAIR, little or no enhancement, and intractable focal epilepsy is the presentation. Excellent outcome after resection. Do not code it as an oligodendroglioma.

full_form: Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor -> Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor (9413)
notes: British spelling; ICD-O-3.2 writes tumor. Code 9413.

full_form: Dysplastic gangliocytoma of cerebellum (Lhermitte-Duclos) -> Dysplastic gangliocytoma of cerebellum (Lhermitte-Duclos) (9493)
notes: 9493 Dysplastic gangliocytoma of cerebellum. Enlarged cerebellar folia with a tigroid striated pattern on MRI. In an adult it is a PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome indicator - Cowden syndrome - and germline PTEN testing should be offered.

alias: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration
full_form: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration -> Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration (9478)
also_known_as: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, NOS
notes: 9478 Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration. The gene locus is written C19MC and is reproduced exactly. C19MC amplification by FISH in more than a tenth of cells is what makes the diagnosis and it overrides histology; LIN28A at 25 per cent or more supports it but a LIN28A-positive, C19MC-negative tumour is ETMR NEC or DICER1-associated, not this code. ICCC-3 files this code in the medulloblastoma subgroup even though it is not a medulloblastoma, so every case inflates that subgroup - report the subgroup with and without it.

alias: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, NOS
full_form: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration -> Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration (9478)
notes: A related term of 9478. Where C19MC amplification was not demonstrated, consider 9473 CNS embryonal tumor, NOS instead and record which tests were unavailable.

full_form: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration -> Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration (9478)
also_known_as: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, NOS
notes: British spelling of the ICD-O-3.2 term, which writes tumor. Code 9478 where C19MC amplification is demonstrated, otherwise 9473 CNS embryonal tumor, NOS.

Retired entity. Cases once called ependymoblastoma are now either 9392 Ependymoma, anaplastic or an embryonal tumour with multilayered rosettes. Code 9392 Ependymoma, anaplastic from an older file and annotate the term as historical; if C19MC amplification is demonstrated the case is 9478 Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration instead.

9391 Ependymoma, NOS is the working code; the site chosen here is the posterior fossa because that is where most childhood ependymomas arise, but the same family occurs supratentorially and in the spinal cord, so enter the compartment the tumour is in. Grade separates 9391 Ependymoma, NOS from 9392 Ependymoma, anaplastic. 9396 Ependymoma, RELA fusion-positive needs FISH or RT-PCR for the fusion; L1CAM and p65 immunohistochemistry can exclude it but cannot assert it. Record GFAP and EMA (dot-like or ring-like) with the result.

full_form: Ependymoma, RELA fusion-positive -> Ependymoma, RELA fusion-positive (9396)
notes: 9396 Ependymoma, RELA fusion-positive is the only molecularly defined ependymoma code ICD-O-3.2 carries, and it uses the gene symbol RELA where WHO CNS5 and cIMPACT-NOW now write ZFTA. The fusion needs FISH or RT-PCR. L1CAM and p65 immunohistochemistry are usable only negatively: double-negative p65 and L1CAM excludes the fusion, but neither marker can assert it. Without a molecular result code 9391 Ependymoma, NOS and record that fusion status was not determined.
Ward and theatre-list abbreviation for ependymoma. Same routing as the full term: 9391 Ependymoma, NOS unless grade or fusion status narrows it.

full_form: Embryonal tumour with multilayered rosettes -> Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration (9478)
also_known_as: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, NOS
notes: Abbreviation for embryonal tumour with multilayered rosettes: 9478 where C19MC amplification is demonstrated. Intraocular medulloepithelioma is not ETMR - C19MC amplification was found in none of 20 such cases despite LIN28A positivity in 19.
9420 Fibrillary astrocytoma. A histological pattern WHO CNS5 folds into diffuse astrocytoma; code it where the report names it and record the pattern.
9532 Fibrous meningioma at behaviour /0. Spindle cells in a collagen-rich matrix; can look like a schwannoma, and EMA and SSTR2A separate them. CNS WHO grade 1.

9492 Gangliocytoma, NOS, CNS WHO grade 1. The local option list carries the name without the trailing NOS, so the pair is not character-identical to ICD-O-3.2, but the code is right. Purely neuronal - mature ganglion cells with NO neoplastic glial component, which is what separates it from 9505 Ganglioglioma, NOS. Synaptophysin, NeuN, neurofilament and chromogranin positive; very low Ki-67.
The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term for 9492, not in local circulation in this exact form and entered so a search finds it.

9505 Ganglioglioma, NOS at behaviour /1, CNS WHO grade 1, or 9505 Ganglioglioma, anaplastic at /3. Two neoplastic components - dysplastic ganglion cells that are synaptophysin and NeuN positive, and a glial component that is GFAP positive; CD34 is often positive and BRAF V600E is common. Temporal lobe, epilepsy.
The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term at behaviour /3 on 9505.
The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term at behaviour /1 on 9505.
Abbreviation for glioblastoma: 9440 Glioblastoma, NOS, or 9441 Giant cell glioblastoma / 9442 Gliosarcoma where the report names the variant.

full_form: Gemistocytic astrocytoma, NOS -> Gemistocytic astrocytoma, NOS (9411)
notes: 9411 Gemistocytic astrocytoma, NOS. The local option list carries this name without the trailing NOS, so the pair does not match ICD-O-3.2 character for character, but the code is the right one. Gemistocytes make up more than a fifth of the tumour cells; the tumour behaves as a diffuse astrocytoma.

full_form: Gemistocytic astrocytoma, NOS -> Gemistocytic astrocytoma, NOS (9411)
notes: The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term for 9411, entered here because it is not in local circulation in this exact form and would otherwise not be searchable.

full_form: Giant cell glioblastoma -> Giant cell glioblastoma (9441)

9421 Pilocytic astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 1 - the commonest childhood brain tumour. It spans compartments: the cerebellum is the commonest paediatric site and is why this alias enters the posterior fossa pathway, but it also arises in the optic pathway and hypothalamus, in the brainstem and in the cord, so set the compartment from the site. Biphasic pattern with Rosenthal fibres and eosinophilic granular bodies; a KIAA1549::BRAF fusion supports it but is not needed to code it.

9425 Pilomyxoid astrocytoma. Classically hypothalamic or chiasmatic in infants - the hypothalamus sits in the supratentorial compartment, which is the pathway this alias enters; it also occurs in the posterior fossa and the cord, so set the compartment from the site. Pinealoma is a misnomer and has no modern equivalent. Krabbe coined it in 1923 for any pineal-region tumour, and it was applied above all to what we now call germinoma — a suprasellar one was called 'ectopic pinealoma'. Russell and Friedman separated germinoma from 'true pinealoma' in 1947, after which the remainder split into pineocytoma and pineoblastoma. So an older file saying 'pinealoma' is as likely to be a GERM CELL TUMOUR, which is Group X and not Group III, as a pineal parenchymal tumour. Order serum and CSF alpha-fetoprotein and beta-human chorionic gonadotropin before coding any pineal-region mass; raised markers make it Group X. Markers are negative in about a third of pineal germ cell tumours, so a negative result does not close the question. WHO CNS5 recognises pineocytoma, pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation, pineoblastoma and papillary tumour of the pineal region — none is called pinealoma. Where the report subclassifies, code the specific entity; where it does not, 8000 Neoplasm, malignant with the site recorded and histopathology documented as outstanding. Topography decides the group: 8000-8005 are IIIf only at C70.0-C72.9 and C75.1-C75.3; at any other site they belong to Group XII.
